extracted.intended_audience: artists, historians, and general readers interested in Leonardo da Vinci's observations on art, nature, and natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing Leonardo da Vinci's short prescriptive and explanatory aphorisms about art, nature, mechanics, perception, and natural philosophy as presented in 'Thoughts on Art and Life'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gravity descends by shortest way to earth's centre
rubrics_metrics.description: A weight with no resistance will descend by the shortest way to the lowest depth, and the lowest depth is the centre of the earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains directness of motion toward the centre; used as a general physical principle describing how bodies fall when unopposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics as the foundation of movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrumental science, that is to say, mechanics, is the most noble and most useful of sciences, inasmuch as by means of it all living bodies which have movement act; and this movement has its origin in the centre of gravity which is placed in the middle, dividing unequal weights, and it has dearth and wealth of muscles and lever also and counter-lever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions mechanics as central to understanding living motion; emphasizes centre of gravity, muscles, levers and counter-levers as explanatory devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat moves moisture; heat underlies life and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat causes moisture to move, and cold arrests it; as is seen in a cold country which arrests the motion of the clouds in the air. Where there is life there is heat, where there is vital heat there is movement of moisture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States a physiological principle linking heat to motion and life; presented as an explanatory natural law rather than an experimental protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect nature's design; do not 'correct' it needlessly
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of cutting out the nostrils of a horse is a piece of ludicrous folly... Nature made two apertures in the nose... nostrils are made to be used when the mouth is employed in masticating its food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues against artificial alteration of natural designs — practical admonition to avoid unnecessary interventions that 'correct' nature without understanding purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants heal and overcompensate after injury
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tree has been stripped of its bark in some spot, nature makes provision for this and gives a greater supply of nourishing sap to the stripped portion than to any other, so that in place of what has been taken away the bark grows thicker than in any other spot. And so impetuous is the motion of the sap that when it reaches the spot which is to be healed, it rises higher like a bounding ball, in bubbles, not unlike boiling water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation of plant physiology used as evidence of nature's restorative mechanisms; suggests careful observation of visible signs (sap, bubbling) to infer internal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaf arrangement serves watering and non-occlusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature has so placed the leaves of the latest shoots of many trees that the sixth leaf is always above the first... firstly, ... the water which feeds the shoot may be able to run down and nourish the bud... Secondly ... one will not be covered by the other, since the five shoots spring on five different sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes phyllotaxy as functional: spacing ensures nourishment of buds and prevents shading; encourages observing form as function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed from known to unknown (use analogues)
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to arrive at knowledge of the motions of birds in the air, it is first necessary to acquire knowledge of the winds, which we will prove by the motions of water in itself, and this knowledge will be a step enabling us to arrive at the knowledge of beings that fly between the air and the wind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological principle: study simpler or better-understood phenomena (water/winds) to infer behavior of more complex ones (flight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate bird flight to insulation, wing structure, and air density
rubrics_metrics.description: Small birds being without down cannot support the intense cold of the high altitudes... small birds, having delicate and thin wings, support themselves in the low air, which is denser, and they could not bear up in the rarer air, which affords slighter resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains flight capability in terms of physiology (down, wing robustness) and environmental physics (air density); use such physical-anatomical reasoning when explaining natural abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wing design: localized pliancy for efficient flight
rubrics_metrics.description: The shafts formed in the shoulders of the wings of birds have been so devised by ingenious nature as to occasion a convenient pliancy in the direct impetus which often occurs in the swift flight of birds, since she found it more practical to bend a small part of the wing in the direct flight than the whole of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design principle: efficient flight is achieved by bending a small portion of the wing (localized flexion) rather than the entire wing; emphasizes observation of structure-function relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward physicians and pharmacological remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Men are chosen to be physicians in order to minister to diseases of which they are ignorant... Take pains to preserve thy health; and thou wilt all the more easily do this if thou avoidest physicians, because their drugs are a kind of alchemy, and there are as many books on this subject as there are on medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates preventive self-care and distrust of contemporary medical practice and remedies, characterized here as quasi-alchemical and unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject claims of perpetual motion and occult engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Oh! meditators on perpetual motion, how many vain projects of similar character you have devised!... and will always happen, to alchemists, who seek to make gold and silver, and to the engineers who wish from still water to obtain life and perpetual motion, and to the supreme fool,--the necromancer and the magician.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general warning against believing or pursuing miraculous mechanical claims (perpetual motion, alchemy, necromancy); emphasizes empirical skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective and visual lines are essential to astronomy and art; mathematics alone cannot give beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no part of astronomy which does not depend on the visual lines and on perspective, the daughter of painting; because the painter is he who by the necessity of his art has begotten perspective... mathematics do the same with their cube roots and square roots, these two sciences deal only with the continuous and discontinuous quantity, but they do not deal with the quality which constitutes the beauty of the works of nature and the ornament of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that visual perspective (an artistic skill) is foundational to accurate astronomical representation and that purely mathematical treatment misses qualitative aspects of beauty; endorses integration of artistic perspective with scientific measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware simplistic natural theories (e.g., quicksilver as seed of metals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lying interpreters of nature affirm that quicksilver is the common seed of all metals. They do not bear in mind that nature raises substances according to the diversity of things which she wishes to produce in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques reductionist or universal explanations that ignore diversity of natural processes; favor explanations sensitive to variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The eye is the most reliable sense for position; ear and smell are less certain
rubrics_metrics.description: The eye in its given distances and by its given means deceives itself in the performance of its functions less than any other sense, because it sees in straight lines which form a cone... But the ear greatly deceives itself as to the position and distance of the objects it apprehends, because the sonorous waves do not reach it in straight lines... The smell is less certain of the spot whence the odour arises, but taste and touch alone come into direct contact with the object which they apprehend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a hierarchy of sensory reliability for localization and identification: vision (most reliable), touch/taste (direct contact), hearing and smell (less reliable); useful methodological guidance when evaluating observations or testimony based on senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothingness exists only in time and words, not in present nature
rubrics_metrics.description: That which is called nothingness is found only in time and in words: in time it is found in the past and future, and not in the present... In time nothingness dwells in the past and the future, and not at all in the present, and in nature it resides among the things which are impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical remark on the concept of nothingness; presented as a conceptual distinction rather than empirical guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirits cannot exist or act as immaterial agents in the elements
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to this matter, we have said... the definition of a spirit is a power united with a body... So according to the definition of weight ... it follows that no element, weighing nothing in its own element, can have weight in the element which is above it... Therefore if it desired to remain in the air it is necessary that it should blend with a quantity of air... it will rarefy that portion of air with which it is mingled... the spirit who would pervade this air would be dismembered or rent and broken up... It is impossible that the spirit, incorporated with a certain quantity of air, should move this air...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out physical and logical arguments against immaterial spirits acting within material elements; includes specific causal reasoning about vacuums, rarefaction, instability, and impossibility of spirits producing independent motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice requires motion/percussion of air against a body
rubrics_metrics.description: The voice is the movement of air in friction against a dense body, or a dense body in friction against the air... Therefore we will say that the spirit cannot produce a voice unless the air be set in motion, but since there is no air within, it cannot discharge what it does not possess... O mathematicians, clear up this error! The spirit cannot have a voice, for where there is a voice there is a body...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines voice in physical terms (air+dense body/friction) and uses that to argue that immaterial spirits cannot speak; useful as a physical criterion for sound production in naturalistic explanations.
